# Paricle deposition (data analysis and visulaization)

This tutorial demostrate how to visulaize fluorescence microscopy and interferometry videos of particle
deposition from evaporating colloidal drops, comparing ellipsoidal and spherical particles, as well
as particles with varying wettability. For this tutorial you will need to download and unzip data and keep in the same working directory. More information about the dataset is available in the README file.

import os
import glob
import subprocess
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.image as mpimg

folder_path = '.'  # <-- Replace this
avi_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(folder_path, '*.avi'))
output_dir = 'temp_frames'

os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

for avi_path in avi_files:
    base = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(avi_path))[0]

    # Get duration of video using ffprobe
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["ffprobe", "-v", "error", "-show_entries",
         "format=duration", "-of",
         "default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1", avi_path],
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT
    )
    duration = float(result.stdout)

    # Calculate time points
    times = [duration * i / 5 for i in range(1, 5)]

    frames = []
    for idx, t in enumerate(times):
        output_img = os.path.join(output_dir, f"{base}_frame{idx+1}.png")
        cmd = [
            "ffmpeg", "-ss", str(t), "-i", avi_path, "-frames:v", "1",
            "-q:v", "2", "-y", output_img
        ]
        subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        frames.append(mpimg.imread(output_img))

    # Plot the frames side by side
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 4))
    for i, frame in enumerate(frames):
        plt.subplot(1, 4, i + 1)
        plt.imshow(frame)
        plt.axis('off')
        plt.title(f'Frame {i + 1}')
    plt.suptitle(base)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
